gloss: to frame someone; to falsely accuse

definitions.gloss: to frame someone; to falsely accuse; to pin the blame on
definitions.explanation: To make an innocent person appear guilty of something they did not do. Literally means "to put wet clothes on someone" — an idiom originating from the idea of being unjustly burdened.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}に{濡|ぬ}れ{衣|ぎぬ}を{着|き}せた。
{無実|むじつ}の{人|ひと}に{濡|ぬ}れ{衣|ぎぬ}を{着|き}せてはいけない。
examples.english: You must not frame an innocent person.

examples.japanese: {同僚|どうりょう}のミスなのに、{私|わたし}が{濡|ぬ}れ{衣|ぎぬ}を{着|き}せられた。
examples.english: Even though it was my colleague's mistake, I was falsely blamed.

notes:
{濡|ぬ}れ{衣|ぎぬ} literally means "wet clothes." The idiom comes from the unpleasant and burdensome feeling of wearing wet clothing — representing the weight of false accusations.

RELATED PATTERNS:
- {濡|ぬ}れ{衣|ぎぬ}を{着|き}せる — to frame someone (active: the accuser's action)
- {濡|ぬ}れ{衣|ぎぬ}を{着|き}せられる — to be framed (passive: the victim's experience)
- {濡|ぬ}れ{衣|ぎぬ}を{着|き}る — to be falsely accused (the victim "wears" the false charge)
- {濡|ぬ}れ{衣|ぎぬ}を{晴|は}らす — to clear one's name

The passive form {着|き}せられる is very common, since speakers more often describe being a victim of false accusation than accusing others.
